newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar catches big updraft from Australian dlr.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar catches big updraft from Australian dlr.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed nearly a U.S. cent up from its lows on Wednesday as it caught a big updraft from the Australian dollar.
The Australian dollar gained sharply in a classic sell-the-rumour-buy-the-fact play after the Reserve Bank of Australia announced a 50 basis point official rate cut.
Dealers said the cut had been discounted by the market and the currency rose on expectations that this was the last in a line of rate cuts.
Further short covering could power the Kiwi higher as long the Australian dollar held most of its gains, dealers said, adding the kiwi had established a new base around 65 U.S. cents.
It closed at 5.00 p.m. (0500 GMT) at US$0.6512/19, down from its 0.6535 high, but well ahead of the 0.6445 low and its 0.6494/01 start.
The Australian dollar rose from a low of US$0.7400 to 0.7455/60. Dealers said there was aggressive buying out of the U.S. in the Australian unit.
Earlier in the session there was buying of the Aussie against the kiwi.

"The kiwi has come back strongly on a combination of short covering, exporter interest, stop losses above 0.6500 and medium-term shorts getting nervous and trimming their positions," a Wellington bank chief dealer said.
"I think we'll trade a range overnight but there is still potential for a little more upside," he said.
Against the Australian dollar, the kiwi ended at A$0.8728/43 from its 0.8700/15 opening. The Trade-Weighted Index finished at 64.98 from its 64.80 opening.
